quote: By the time of the Civil War farms in the area that would later be occupied by the national military park ranged from 10 to 240 acres with an average size of 128 acres
says: Farms of the park area ranged from 10 to 240 acres, average 128 acres; the smaller farms lay on Cemetery Ridge, the larger along McPherson Ridge and the lower ground between Seminary and Cemetery Ridge.

quote: Wheat output dropped to third place behind corn and oats
says: By 1860 the farmers of the Gettysburg area had cut wheat output so that it stood third, behind corn and oats; more land went to pasture and hay.
note: A statement about output in 1860, not about the fields of July 1863; used with the damage-claim acreages to set the prior mix of crops.

quote: an occasional plot of buckwheat small potato patch small apple or peach orchard and small tracts of grassland for hay and pasture
says: By July 1863 the farms were a patchwork of small fields of corn, oats, wheat and rye, with an occasional plot of buckwheat, a small potato patch, a small apple or peach orchard and small tracts of grassland for hay and pasture.
note: The per-farm acreages that follow in the printed sentence are lost in the saved text.

quote: In the 19th century farmers began to plant small orchards consisting mostly of apple trees but some groves contained peaches as well as cherry pear plum and quince trees
says: Orchards of the district were mostly apple, with some peach, cherry, pear, plum and quince.
note: The weights are not in the source; they are a stated reading of 'mostly apple, some peach, cherry, pear, plum, quince' and are marked inferred wherever used.

quote: Woodlots were another crop farmers harvested They provided fuel building materials and place to hunt game for the farm
says: Woodlots were harvested for fuel and building materials.

quote: Most woodlots followed ridgelines such as Warfield and Seminary Ridge although one exception is Cemetery Ridge that was mostly under cultivation
says: Most woodlots followed the ridgelines (Warfield and Seminary Ridge); Cemetery Ridge was mostly cultivated.

quote: Typically the understory was open and cleared as result of these uses
says: The understory of the farm woodlots was typically open and cleared.
note: Applies to farm woodlots; not stated for Culp's Hill, Big Round Top or the Plum Run thickets.

quote: Maintain meadow and pasture felds as a mix of grasses, wildfowers, and other forbs to create the patchwork appearance of crop, pasture, and hay felds present in 1863
says: The park's own treatment standard describes 1863 as a patchwork of crop, pasture and hay fields; meadows and pastures were a mix of grasses and wildflowers.

quote: In 1863, woodlands and thickets covered marginal lands that could not be farmed, used for pasture, or maintained as woodlots
says: Woodland and thickets covered the marginal lands that could not be farmed, pastured or kept as woodlots.

quote: Many orchards dotted the 1863 landscape because tree fruits provided a valuable food source for subsistence farmers and for livestock
says: Many orchards dotted the 1863 landscape.

quote: Individual trees dotted the 1863 Gettysburg battlefeld, many of which were located in dooryards, in felds near rock outcroppings, along fence lines, and along boundary lines
says: Single trees stood in dooryards, in fields near rock outcrops, along fence lines and along boundaries.

quote: Grazing by cattle and hogs within the deciduous woodlot resulted in scarce understory at the time of the battle
says: The deciduous David Blocher Woods had a scarce understory in July 1863 because cattle and hogs grazed in it.

quote: the park’s 1863 period plan notes the Gilbert Orchard was a young or immature orchard at the time of the battle
says: The Gilbert Orchard was young or immature in July 1863.

quote: No specifc army command was cited for additional damage to or destruction of 30 acres of wheat in two separate felds, 22–26 acres of oats, and two acres of barley
says: The Josiah Benner farm held 30 acres of wheat in two fields, 22-26 acres of oats, two acres of barley and (a claim against the Eleventh Corps) two acres of corn.

quote: Munshower Field was open in July 1863 and probably used as meadow or pasture
says: Munshower Field was open in July 1863 and probably meadow or pasture.
note: The anchor is only the neighbourhood the CLR gives (the cleared field south of Wheatfield Road, beside the Little Round Top tract): an inference, radius 260 m.

quote: The woody growth obscured an open area that contained crops and meadow at the time of the battle
says: William Patterson Fields 1-3, west of the Taneytown Road and north of Wheatfield Road, held crops and meadow in 1863.

quote: Through this swale trickled a small stream, at that time nearly dry
says: The stream through Abraham Spangler's Spring Meadow was nearly dry at the time of the battle.

quote: primarily devoid of woody vegetation at the time of the battle
says: Spangler's Spring Meadow had almost no woody growth at the time of the battle.

quote: The Codori and Trostle Thickets grew into a forested area along Plum Run and extended into felds that had been open during the battle
says: Fields beside Plum Run that are now thicket were open in July 1863.
feature: Codori and Trostle fields beside Plum Run
note: A statement about modern growth: it forbids drawing the modern thicket's extent in 1863.

quote: The Codori and Trostle Woodlots appear as a single mass of managed vegetation but consist of two similar and adjoining features from 1863
says: The Codori and Trostle woodlots were two separate adjoining woodlots in 1863.

quote: The Jacob and Emanuel Weikert Woods appear as a single mass of managed vegetation but consist of two similar and adjoining features from 1863
says: The Jacob and Emanuel Weikert woods were two adjoining woodlots in 1863.

quote: had limited military value since its slopes were covered by a mature deciduous and partially coniferous forest, preventing observation
says: Big Round Top's slopes were covered by a mature forest, deciduous and partly coniferous, that prevented observation.

quote: The fences of the 1863 Gettysburg landscape were mostly wood or wood and stone, and predominantly American chestnut and black locust
says: The fences were mostly of American chestnut and black locust: both species grew in the district in 1863.
note: Evidence of species present, not of their share in any woodlot.

quote: young apple and peach orchard (with a great variety of fruit in the yard)
says: An 1859 advertisement of the Forney farm listed a young apple and peach orchard and a great variety of fruit in the yard.

quote: The orchards in my front and towards my right were very thick orchards, and a very heavy force of skirmishers could get pretty well into them without being seen
says: On 2 July the orchards in front of a Union general's right were so thick that a heavy force of skirmishers could get into them unseen.
feature: orchards at the Klingel and Rogers farms
note: Testimony quoted by the NPS record; the speaker's identity is in that report.

quote: the Bushman and Weikert tracts on the east slopes of Li le Round Top were wooded in July 1863
says: The Bushman and Weikert tracts on the east slopes of Little Round Top were wooded in July 1863.

quote: Hanaway Tract (tract on western slope of Li le Round Top, cleared of most trees prior to 1863)
says: The Hanaway tract on the west slope of Little Round Top was cleared of most trees before 1863.
note: The NPS report says 'most trees': a few remained; the open polygon of the repository's land-cover layer carries the outline.

quote: Tree line at summit of Li le Round Top dividing Hanaway Tract from wooded east-slope tracts
says: A tree line at the summit of Little Round Top divided the cleared west slope from the wooded east-slope tracts.

quote: In 1863 Big and Little Round Tops constituted a significant woodland area in the vicinity of Gettysburg
says: In 1863 Big and Little Round Top together were a significant woodland.

quote: by 1863 most woodlands had been cleared for farm land or pasture
says: By 1863 most woodland of the district had been cleared for farmland or pasture.

quote: This included loss of livestock and crops including four tons of hay, 9 acres of wheat, 16 acres of corn, 4 acres of oats, 18 acres of grass, and a half acre of potatoes
says: The McPherson farm (tenant Slentz) lost crops: 9 acres of wheat, 16 of corn, 4 of oats, 18 of grass, half an acre of potatoes and 4 tons of hay.

quote: James Wills claimed the loss of 800 fence panels, 19 acres of corn, two 15-acre fields of wheat, 15 acres of oats, and a field of grass
says: The Wills farm lost 19 acres of corn, two 15-acre fields of wheat, 15 acres of oats and a field of grass.

quote: William Comfort, the Harman tenant, claimed the loss of 10 acres of wheat and 5 acres of rye, along with 11 cattle
says: The Harman farm (tenant Comfort) lost 10 acres of wheat and 5 of rye.

quote: resulting in loss of 20 bushels of wheat, 15 bushels of corn, and 13 acres of pasture
says: Abraham Spangler's fields south of the pike lost 13 acres of pasture, with wheat and corn in bushels.

quote: cited the loss of 32 acres of wheat, 30 acres of timothy grass, 10 acres of oats, and the partial destruction of 10 acres of corn
says: The Forney farm lost 32 acres of wheat, 30 of timothy grass, 10 of oats and part of 10 acres of corn.

quote: John Slyder claimed damage to or destruction of 5–7 acres of wheat, 4 acres of corn, 2 acres of grass, and a ton of hay in the barn
says: The Slyder farm lost 5-7 acres of wheat, 4 of corn and 2 of grass; the Bushman farm lost wheat, oats, corn, rye and hay grass (acreage not given).

quote: Michael Bushman submitted a damage claim citing an unspecifed amount of wheat, oats, corn, rye, and hay grass destroyed
says: The Bushman farm had wheat, oats, corn, rye and hay grass (acreages not stated).

quote: Rose Wheatfeld is bounded on the north by Wheatfeld Road, on the east by Houck Field, on the south by Rose Woods, and on the west by Rose West Woods and Rose Lane Gap
says: The Rose Wheatfield was bounded by Wheatfield Road on the north, Houck Field on the east, Rose Woods on the south, and Rose West Woods and Rose Lane Gap on the west.

neighbours.W: Rose West Woods and Rose Lane Gap

quote: Fence lines along the north and west perimeters of the Rose Wheatfeld are documented as a wooden fence in the 1863 Bachelder Map and as worm fence in the 1868 Warren Map
says: The north and west boundaries of the Rose Wheatfield were fenced (wooden fence on Bachelder's map, worm fence on Warren's).
